researcher: Codex parallel cyprus-georgia research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Human History Map, imported civilization index and historical border snapshots
sources.note: Primary project data were checked locally for exact IDs, names, aliases, date intervals and every historical TopoJSON feature. Cyprus-1960 is distinct from medieval cyprus and modern northern-cyprus; georgia-1994 is distinct from medieval georgia. Point tests and bounds are preserved in this bundle's identity audit. Imported shapes are display data, not legal boundary or effective-control surveys.

sources.title: Human History Map, modern GeoJSON
sources.note: Primary project GeoJSON was checked locally. The modern file gives Cyprus separate cyprus-1960 and northern-cyprus features but does not reliably excise the British Sovereign Base Areas; the Georgia feature includes tested points at Sukhumi and Tskhinvali. Point tests are aids to disclose geometry, not geopolitical findings.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Series, Treaty concerning the Establishment of the Republic of Cyprus
sources.note: Original treaty text checked for the Republic's establishment on 16 August 1960, the territory excluded from the Republic, continued United Kingdom sovereignty over Akrotiri and Dhekelia, and the accompanying declaration on administration of the Sovereign Base Areas.

sources.title: Republic of Cyprus, Constitution as amended through 2013
sources.note: Official English text checked for Article 1's independent sovereign republic and Greek president/Turkish vice-president design, Article 2's community definitions, and the extensive power-sharing structure. Constitutional design is distinguished from later practice.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, mandate
sources.note: Official UN mission account checked for the December 1963 intercommunal violence, Security Council Resolution 186 and UNFICYP's establishment in March 1964, the original mandate, and the 16 August 1974 de facto ceasefire.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, about UNFICYP
sources.note: Official UN account checked for the 1974 coup favouring union with Greece, the subsequent Turkish military intervention, Turkish forces' control in the north, the ceasefire lines and UN buffer zone. UN wording is retained rather than substituting a legal conclusion.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, events of 1974
sources.note: Official UN chronology checked for Security Council Resolution 353, the 16 August 1974 ceasefire, displacement and humanitarian need. Contemporary estimates are presented as dated UN reporting, not exact final totals.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, the buffer zone
sources.note: Official mission page checked for the roughly 180-kilometre buffer zone, varying width, post-1974 separation, civilian-use areas, crossings since 2003 and the mixed village of Pyla. The page was updated 22 November 2025.

sources.title: United Nations Security Council Resolution 541 (1983)
sources.note: Original UN resolution checked for its 18 November 1983 date, conclusion that the northern declaration was legally invalid, call for withdrawal of that declaration, and call on states not to recognize any Cypriot state other than the Republic of Cyprus.

sources.title: European Union, Protocol No. 10 on Cyprus
sources.note: Primary EU legal text checked for suspension of the acquis in areas where the Government of the Republic of Cyprus does not exercise effective control and the Council mechanism for changing that suspension after a settlement.

sources.title: European Court of Auditors, Special Report No. 6/2012 on assistance to the Turkish Cypriot community
sources.note: Official EU audit checked for Cyprus joining the European Union on 1 May 2004, the whole island legally being EU territory, and suspension of the acquis in the north because the Republic's government does not exercise effective control there.

sources.title: European Court of Human Rights, Djavit An v. Turkey judgment
sources.note: Primary judgment checked for the Court's application of its earlier Cyprus case law: Turkey's armed forces exercised effective overall control of northern Cyprus and Convention responsibility extended to acts of the subordinate local administration. This jurisdictional holding is not a border survey.

sources.title: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 1489 (XV), Admission of the Republic of Cyprus
sources.note: Original UN record checked for the Republic of Cyprus being admitted to United Nations membership on 20 September 1960. Membership is a legal-institutional fact, not evidence that constitutional power sharing functioned as planned.

sources.title: Republic of Cyprus Press and Information Office, Cyprus at a Glance 2024
sources.note: Official trilingual publication checked for the modern state names Κυπριακή Δημοκρατία, Kıbrıs Cumhuriyeti and Republic of Cyprus. The card identifies the Greek and Turkish scripts and treats the Greek transliteration as editorial.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Choirokoitia
sources.note: Official World Heritage record checked for seventh- to fifth-millennium BCE occupation, circular stone and mud-brick houses, courtyard activity, hearths and basins, burials under floors, finds and conservation. The site is prehistoric heritage in Cyprus, not an achievement of the 1960 republic.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Lefkara laces or Lefkaritika
sources.note: UNESCO's inscription checked for four main lace techniques, women working socially in village streets, mothers and grandmothers teaching girls, and the practice's role in identity and livelihoods. It is a living tradition, not a universal household routine.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Tsiattista poetic duelling
sources.note: UNESCO's inscription checked for improvised rhyming couplet contests in the Greek Cypriot dialect, accompaniment by violin or lute, performance at weddings and fairs, and the demand for wit under time pressure. Community scope is kept explicit.

sources.title: Cyprus Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth, State Institutes of Further Education
sources.note: Official ministry page checked for the institutes' network, afternoon and evening language teaching, and free Greek classes for Turkish Cypriots and Turkish classes for Greek Cypriots since 2003. Published counts are treated as page-era figures.

sources.title: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies, Cyprus: Health System Summary 2024
sources.note: Authoritative WHO-hosted system summary checked for the 2019 introduction of GeSY, near-universal coverage, lower out-of-pocket spending, mixed public/private delivery and continuing sustainability, quality, workforce and data challenges.

sources.title: Republic of Cyprus Water Development Department, recycled water
sources.note: Official department page checked for tertiary treatment of municipal wastewater, reuse mainly for irrigation and recharge, separate distribution, and operating rules. Reuse volumes vary by year and are omitted from the card.

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia, Act of Restoration of State Independence of Georgia, English text
sources.note: Primary legal text checked for the 9 April 1991 act, its reliance on the 31 March referendum, restoration based on the 26 May 1918 act and its declarations of independence and territorial integrity. The act's historical argument is identified as the act's own legal framing.

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia, Act of Restoration of State Independence, Georgian original
sources.note: Official Georgian original checked for the exact title საქართველოს სახელმწიფოებრივი დამოუკიდებლობის აღდგენის აქტი and its 9 April 1991 date. The card provides a close English translation and identifies modern Mkhedruli script.

sources.title: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 46/241, Admission of the Republic of Georgia
sources.note: Original UN record checked for Georgia's admission to United Nations membership on 31 July 1992 under the then-used formal name Republic of Georgia. The card does not confuse UN admission with the 1991 independence act.

sources.title: United Nations, Georgia institutional profile
sources.note: Official UN profile checked for 1991 independence, the 1991-1992 South Ossetia conflict and ceasefire, the 1992-1993 Abkhazia war and mass displacement. It is used for dated early-state chronology, not as a current control map.

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia, Constitution of Georgia
sources.note: Current official English text checked for adoption on 24 August 1995, the referendum and independence-act basis, and Article 1's independent, unified and indivisible state. Constitutional territory is distinguished from effective control.

sources.title: OSCE/ODIHR, Georgia parliamentary elections 2003
sources.note: Official OSCE election record checked for serious irregularities in the November 2003 parliamentary elections, mass protests, President Eduard Shevardnadze's resignation and cancellation of the proportional contest. 'Rose Revolution' is used as the common name, not an OSCE endorsement.

sources.title: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, observation of Georgia's 2012 parliamentary elections
sources.note: Official observer report checked for the 2012 election, opposition victory, President Saakashvili's concession, the first peaceful transfer of power through the ballot box and documented polarization and campaign shortcomings.

sources.title: European Court of Human Rights, Georgia v. Russia (II), Grand Chamber judgment
sources.note: Primary judgment checked for the 8-12 August 2008 active hostilities, 12 August ceasefire agreement, subsequent Russian effective control over South Ossetia and Abkhazia, and continued presence. This Convention-jurisdiction finding is dated and not a settlement of sovereignty.

sources.title: European Court of Human Rights, Georgia v. Russia (IV), judgment on borderisation
sources.note: Official Court release checked for the 9 April 2024 merits judgment on hardened administrative boundary lines since 2009, blocked access to homes, land and families, and denial of Georgian-language education, plus the 14 October 2025 just-satisfaction judgment. Victim and award totals are omitted.

sources.title: European Court of Human Rights, Mamasakhlisi and Others v. Georgia and Russia
sources.note: Official Court release checked for the 19 December 2023 judgment: Abkhazia was outside the Georgian government's de facto control while Russia exercised continued effective control there. The Court's jurisdictional analysis is not recast as recognition of sovereignty.

sources.title: European External Action Service, The European Union and Georgia
sources.note: Official EU overview checked for candidate status granted on 14 December 2023, the EU assessment that the accession process was de facto halted in June 2024 and remained at a standstill, support for internationally recognized territorial integrity, and EUMM presence.

sources.title: OSCE/ODIHR, Georgia parliamentary elections 2024 final report
sources.note: Official final-report page checked for concerns about voter pressure, weakened institutional independence, restrictions on fundamental freedoms, compromised ability to vote without fear and suppression of post-election protests. It does not itself void or validate the result.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, living culture of three writing systems of the Georgian alphabet
sources.note: UNESCO's inscription checked for the Mrgvlovani, Nuskhuri and Mkhedruli systems, modern educational use of Mkhedruli, ecclesiastical use of older forms and transmission through schools, families and craftspeople.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Georgian wheat culture: traditions and rituals
sources.note: UNESCO's 2025 inscription checked for local wheat varieties, planting and harvest practices, stone mills and ovens, ritual breads for births, weddings and funerals, and family/community transmission. Role descriptions are not universalized to every household.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Georgian polyphonic singing
sources.note: UNESCO record checked for regional polyphonic forms, songs linked with work, festivities and healing, the krimanchuli or cockerel's-crow upper voice, and threats from rural migration and declining contexts of transmission.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, ancient Georgian traditional qvevri wine-making method
sources.note: UNESCO decision and nomination summary checked for egg-shaped clay qvevri buried in the ground, family and neighbour participation, five- to six-month fermentation and intergenerational transmission. The card treats wine as an adult drink and children as learners of craft and agriculture.

sources.title: Georgian National Museum, Dmanisi Museum-Reserve guide
sources.note: Official museum guide checked for approximately 1.8-million-year-old hominin remains, extinct animals, stone tools, the archaeological field museum and educational work. The card rejects any equation between ancient hominins and modern national identity.

sources.title: UNICEF Georgia, early steps in bilingual education in kindergartens
sources.note: Official UNICEF account checked for the bilingual preschool programme begun in 2020, its 2024 reach to 34 kindergartens in ethnic-minority regions, use of Georgian alongside children's home languages, and teacher/family experiences.

sources.title: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies, Georgia: Health System Review 2023
sources.note: Authoritative WHO-hosted review checked for the 2013 universal health coverage programme, reduced out-of-pocket burden and remaining low public spending, co-payments, outpatient medicine costs and unequal access.

sources.title: WHO Europe, viral hepatitis elimination centre opens in Georgia
sources.note: Official WHO account checked for the national hepatitis C elimination programme launched in 2015 and, by January 2023, more than 2.8 million people screened, more than 80,000 treated and a reported cure rate above 99 percent among treated patients.

sources.title: WHO Europe, turning telemedicine into a core health service in Georgia
sources.note: Official WHO update checked for telemedicine equipment in 60 rural clinics, links to distant specialists and the continuing legal, funding and workforce work needed to make pilots a durable national service.

sources.title: UNICEF, Children and Adolescent Rights in Georgia 2025
sources.note: Official UNICEF situation analysis checked for household drinking-water contamination and low shares of surveyed public schools meeting functional clean sanitation standards, with worse conditions for rural and poorer children. Survey scope and date are stated.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Indexed identity is Cyprus, alias Republic of Cyprus, approximately 1960-open, with intervals 1960-1994, 1994-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020 and 2020-2100. It is not medieval cyprus (800-1530) and does not absorb the separate northern-cyprus record. World-1960 bounds are [32.14292142921431,34.539018472550026,34.457744577445794,35.6447281853884]; tests include both Nicosia points and Morphou but exclude Kyrenia and Famagusta, so the feature cannot represent post-1974 control. The identical 1994, 2000 and 2010 feature has bounds [32.14292142921431,34.53882550812238,33.67653676536767,35.156070337311625] and excludes both tested Nicosia points and Famagusta, reducing the record to a southwest fragment. The modern cyprus-1960 feature has bounds [32.257,34.572,34.005,35.173] and includes tested points in Akrotiri and Dhekelia even though the 1960 treaty excludes both British Sovereign Base Areas. Modern northern-cyprus is a separate polygon with bounds [32.732,35,34.576,35.672]. No imported polygon is treated as a legal frontier or reliable effective-control map.

Indexed identity is modern Georgia, approximately 1994-open, with intervals 1994-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020 and 2020-2100. The inherited alias Kingdom of Georgia conflicts with the era and is not used as identity evidence; medieval georgia (1000-1530) remains a separate card. The identical 1994, 2000 and 2010 feature has bounds [40.0990009900099,41.05899769700155,46.816668166681666,43.590818681888656]; tests include Tbilisi, Batumi, Tskhinvali and Akhalkalaki but exclude Sukhumi. The modern feature has bounds [39.955,41.064,46.638,43.553] and includes both Sukhumi and Tskhinvali, matching claimed territory rather than effective administration.
